# Combine MatrixEQTL chromosomes for each treatment-celltype
The matrixEQTL results are in the /project/gilad/geena/ALK_analysis/results/control/matrixeqtl_single/ or /treatment/matrixeqtl_single/ folders.
Once I input the result folder names I want to use I:
1) Combine the chromosomes since I ran matrixeqtl on each chr separately  (saved under /results/matrixeqtl_combined_results/<folder_name>/*combine_chr/*)
2) Calculate SE and reformat as fastQTL format and output into compressed .gz files (saved under /results/matrixeqtl_combined_results/<folder_name>/*fastqtl_like/*)


# Reformat as FastQTL
Combine chromosomes for each celltype-condition and save in /project/gilad/geena/ALK_analysis/results/matrixeqtl_combined_results/update_3.13.25/combine_chr

Get all cell types in common between control and treatment

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(data.table)

# Define paths for control and treatment results
control_folder <- "/project/gilad/geena/publication_clean/results/control/matrixeqtl/medianUMI1_updated4.29.26"
treatment_folder <- "/project/gilad/geena/publication_clean/results/treatment/matrixeqtl/medianUMI1_updated4.29.26"

# List all files
control_files <- list.files(control_folder, pattern = "_cis.txt$", full.names = FALSE)
treatment_files <- list.files(treatment_folder, pattern = "_cis.txt$", full.names = FALSE)

# Function to extract cell type from filenames
extract_cell_type <- function(filenames) {
  cell_types <- sub("^[^_]+_", "", filenames)  # Remove the first part (treatment or "Control")
  cell_types <- sub("_chr[0-9XY]+_cis.txt$", "", cell_types)  # Remove chromosome info and suffix
  unique(cell_types)  # Return unique cell types
}

# Get cell types from control and treatment
control_cell_types <- extract_cell_type(control_files) # 26 cell types
treatment_cell_types <- extract_cell_type(treatment_files) 

# Find common cell types
common_cell_types <- intersect(control_cell_types, treatment_cell_types)
print("Cell types in common between treatment and control analysis:")
print(common_cell_types)

```

```{r}
# Define conditions, chromosomes, and output directory
conditions <- c("Control", "Ale", "Bri", "Cer", "Cri", "Lor")
chromosomes <- paste0("chr", 1:22)  # Chromosomes 1-22

# Define the output folder for combined results
combined_folder <- "/project/gilad/geena/publication_clean/results/combined/medianUMI1/combine_chr/"
if (!dir.exists(combined_folder)) dir.create(combined_folder, recursive = TRUE)

# Iterate over cell types and conditions
for (cell_type in common_cell_types) {
  for (condition in conditions) {
    # Set input folder based on condition
    input_folder <- ifelse(condition == "Control", control_folder, treatment_folder) # control_folder and treatment_folder set in previous chunk
    
    combined_results <- list()  # Store results
    
    for (chr in chromosomes) {
      input_file <- file.path(input_folder, paste0(condition, "_", cell_type, "_", chr, "_cis.txt"))
      
      if (file.exists(input_file)) {
        chr_data <- fread(input_file)
        
        if (nrow(chr_data) > 0) {
          combined_results[[chr]] <- chr_data
          print(paste0("Loaded: ", condition, " ", cell_type, " ", chr))
        } else {
          print(paste0("File is empty for: ", condition, " ", cell_type, " ", chr))
        }
      } else {
        print(paste0("File not found: ", input_file))
      }
    }
    
    # Combine results and save
    if (length(combined_results) > 0) {
      all_data <- bind_rows(combined_results)
      output_file <- file.path(combined_folder, paste0(condition, "_", cell_type, "_combined_cis.txt"))
      write_tsv(all_data, file = output_file, col_names = TRUE)
      print(paste0("Saved combined results for: ", condition, " ", cell_type))
    } else {
      print(paste0("No valid data found for: ", condition, " ", cell_type))
    }
  }
}

```


Now that the chromosomes are combined for each treatment-condition, reformat to match fastQTL format in order to use fastQTL2mash code.

NOTE: Wenhe found that when calculating standard error we need to use p-value rather than t-value at our (smaller) sample sizes which can lead to more false positives because SE is underestimated

mash assumes normal distribution, and input to mash is beta and SE; in smaller sample sizes when t-statistic skewed, then using SE = beta/t can lead to oversignificance (false positives) bc SE is underestimated; affects smaller sample size -> instead of using beta/t, use beta and p-value


```{r}
# Define input and output folders
input_folder <- "/project/gilad/geena/publication_clean/results/combined/medianUMI1/combine_chr/"
output_folder <- "/project/gilad/geena/publication_clean/results/combined/medianUMI1/fastqtl_like/"

# Create output folder if it doesn't exist
if (!dir.exists(output_folder)) {
  dir.create(output_folder, recursive = TRUE)
}

# Define conditions and cell types
conditions <- c("Control", "Ale", "Bri", "Cer", "Cri", "Lor")

# Iterate over cell types and conditions
for (cell_type in common_cell_types) {
  for (condition in conditions) {
    # Construct the input file path
    input_file <- paste0(input_folder, condition, "_", cell_type, "_combined_cis.txt")
    
    # Check if the file exists
    if (file.exists(input_file)) {
      # Read the combined file
      results <- fread(input_file) %>%
        # NOTE: use p-value not t-value
        mutate(se_beta=abs(beta/qnorm(pvalue/2))) %>%  # Calculate standard error
        dplyr::select(gene, snps, beta, se_beta, pvalue) %>%  # Select required columns
        na.omit() %>%  # Remove rows with missing values
        arrange(gene)  # Sort by gene
      
      # Construct the output file path
      output_file <- paste0(output_folder, cell_type, "_", condition, "_formash.out.gz")
      
      # Write the results to the output file
      write_tsv(results, file = output_file, col_names = TRUE, quote = "none")
      print(paste0("Processed: ", cell_type, " ", condition))
    } else {
      print(paste0("File not found: ", input_file))
    }
  }
}
```


# Create list files
Instead of looking just at mash within cell types across conditions, I can look at all conditions and cell types jointly (in input file) and then once I run mash, it will create an output for each celltype_condition column and then depending on whether I want to look at sharing across treatments or sharing across cell types then I can just subset the columns. In order to do this there needs to be more genes shared across cell types (so more lenient gene filtering?).

In order to do this I created a .list file called all_treatments_joint.list that included all celltype x treatment combinations, for example:

This was the code I used locally to create a file with all treatment_celltype combinations so that I can run mash jointly across all cell types and treatments
```{r}
# Define input folder
input_folder <- "/project/gilad/geena/publication_clean/results/combined/medianUMI1/fastqtl_like"

# List all files (only filenames, no full path)
files <- list.files(input_folder, full.names = FALSE)

# Create the full paths
new_paths <- file.path(input_folder, files)

# Replace spaces with underscores
#files_clean <- gsub(" ", "_", files)
#new_paths <- file.path(input_folder, files_clean)

# Save to list
writeLines(new_paths, "/project/gilad/geena/publication_clean/code/fastqtl2mash/medianUMI1.list")

```

# Check mash input
```{r}
library(data.table)

# Read your all_treatments_joint.list
list_file <- "/project/gilad/geena/publication_clean/code/fastqtl2mash/medianUMI1.list"
files <- readLines(list_file)

# Extract gene sets
gene_sets <- lapply(files, function(f) {
  fread(f, select = "gene")$gene
})

names(gene_sets) <- basename(files)

shared_genes_all <- Reduce(intersect, gene_sets)
length(shared_genes_all)

```
